title: Science Over Shortcuts: ETHealthworld’s NutriWell Conclave to Decode India’s Changing Nutrition Story
summary: India’s nutrition and wellness landscape is witnessing a growing interest in supplements, weight management, personalised nutrition and AI-driven health recommendations, raising concerns around misinformation, unverified claims and evidence-based practices....

contentHtml:
New Delhi: India’s nutrition and wellness landscape is growing at an unprecedented pace, driven by increasing health awareness among consumers and a more proactive approach to well-being and preventive healthcare.The growing conversation around weight management, supplements, gut health, immunity and personalised nutrition demands stronger scientific evidence, responsible self-care and informed consumer choices.

Ahead of the conclave, ETHealthworld has been exploring these questions through a special edition newsletter, bringing together news features, interviews and authored articles from leading voices in nutrition. We have raised questions such as: Can regulation keep pace with the nutraceutical boom? What do GLP-1 drugs and AI mean for the way India eats? And why are we eating more but nourishing less? Read the full newsletter here.

Advt

These questions will take centre stage at the third edition of the ETHealthworld NutriWell Conclave & Awards 2026, under the theme “Rewriting India’s Nutrition Story – Science Over Shortcuts”.The conclave will bring together policymakers, regulatory authorities, scientists, nutritionists, clinicians and industry leaders to examine emerging trends in nutrition, the evolving science of weight management, the growing influence of GLP-1 drugs, and the role of technology and food innovation in shaping India's nutrition ecosystem.

The discussions will also explore the relationship between gut and brain health, responsible self-care, the growing role of structured nutrition in managing health conditions, and the need to address misinformation in the wellness industry.

The third edition of the annual conclave features Bayer as associate partner, Dr. Reddy’s and Nestlé Health Science as wellness partners, Nestlé as nutrition partner, Rivadu Lifesciences as supporting partner and OmniActive as branding partner.

The conclave will commence with welcome remarks by Prathiba Raju, Associate Editor, ETHealthworld. The welcome address will set the stage for the inaugural panel discussion, Rewriting India’s Nutrition Story – Science Over Shortcuts.The panel will bring together Dr. Amit Sharma, Executive Director, FSSAI; Dr. G.M. Subba Rao, Scientist-G, ICMR-NIN; Dr. Kashipa Harit, Joint Director, NABH; Dr. Bani Tamber Aeri, Professor, Department of Food and Nutrition, Institute of Home Economics, Delhi University; Prof. Pushpesh Pant, Indian food critic and historian; and Dr. Sarath Gopalan, President, Nutrition Society of India.

Advt

The discussion will be moderated by Vikas Dandekar, Editor-Pharma and Healthcare, The Economic Times Group.The conversation will then shift to the role of regulation in shaping India's nutrition future, with a plenary address and fireside session by Rajit Punhani, CEO, FSSAI.From the broader questions of food safety and regulation, the focus will move to an increasingly important aspect of preventive healthcare: how structured nutrition can support sustainable weight management.This will be followed by a session on The Missing Piece in Weight Management: The Role of Structured Nutrition. The session will be moderated by Ambika Nair, Clinical Nutritionist, Sehat Plus, Pune; Director, My Nutritional Needs; and Secretary, Indian Dietetic Association.

Advt

Panelists include Sandhya Pandey, General Manager and Chief Dietician, Medanta Hospital, Gurugram; Sheryl Salis, Founder and Director, Nurture Health Solutions and Nurture Health Academy and Research Centre; and Aishwarya Kumbhakoni, Consultant Dietician, Diabetes, Kokilaben Dhirubhai Ambani Hospital, Mumbai.As consumers increasingly turn to supplements and over-the-counter wellness products, the question of responsible self-care becomes equally important. The focus will then shift to this subject, with Sandeep Verma, Country Head, Bayer Consumer Health, delivering a session on Science Over Shortcuts: Building a Culture of Responsible Self-Care. Vikas Dandekar, Editor-Pharma and Healthcare, The Economic Times Group, will moderate the session.

The discussion on weight management will continue after the networking luncheon, this time examining the growing influence of GLP-1 drugs and the questions they raise for healthcare, patients and the nutrition industry.The programme will resume with a panel discussion titled GLP-1s: Are They Creating a Health Crisis or Creating a New Market?Panelists include Dr. Rohit Warrier, Communications Director, American Diabetes Association; Dr. Anuj Maheshwari, President, RSSDI; Dr. Rajesh Rajput, Director and Head, Division of Endocrinology and Diabetes, Medanta, Gurugram; and Dr. Anil Arora, Senior Consultant, Institute of Liver, Gastroenterology and Pancreatico Biliary Sciences. The discussion will be moderated by Vikas Dandekar, Editor-Pharma and Healthcare, The Economic Times Group.Beyond medicines and clinical interventions, technology and food innovation are also influencing how consumers make nutrition choices. The conclave will next examine this intersection through a panel titled The New Nutrition Equation: AI, Food Innovation and the Changing Indian Consumer.The panel will feature Dr. Mona Duggal, Scientist-G and Director, ICMR National Institute for Research in Digital Health; Dr. Ganesh Bagler, Head and Professor, Computational Biology, IIIT-Delhi; Dr. Naval Kishore Vikram, Professor of Medicine and Head, Medicine Unit 2, AIIMS New Delhi; Ruchika Jain, Chief Dietician, Fortis Vasant Kunj; and Shilpa Wadhwa, Head-Nutrition, Health and Wellness, Nestlé India Limited. The discussion will be moderated by Prathiba Raju, Associate Editor, ETHealthworld.After a networking break, the conclave will turn to another emerging area of nutrition science the relationship between gut health and brain health. With growing consumer interest in the gut-brain connection, the discussion will examine how much of the emerging science is backed by evidence and where consumer claims may be running ahead of research.The session, titled Gut-Brain Health: Balancing Promising Science with Rapid Consumerisation, will feature Ishi Khosla, Clinical Nutritionist, Author, Researcher and Columnist; Shreyasi Agarwal, CEO, Development Chamber of Food and Agriculture Trade Association (DeFacto India); Dr. Manjari Chandra, Functional Nutritionist, Influencer, Author and Speaker; and Dr. Prasun Chatterjee, Group Clinical Lead, Geriatrics, Apollo Hospitals. The discussion will be moderated by Prathiba Raju, Associate Editor, ETHealthworld.The conclave will be followed in the evening by the ETHealthworld Nutrition and Wellness Awards.
